key_findings.depset_equality: Depset == is NestedSet identity in Bazel 9.3 (depset([1]) == depset([1]) is False; empty depsets of an order are equal), so structs holding separately created depsets are not deduplicated (run 1 MISMATCH; fixed).
key_findings.traversal: each NestedSet node keeps its own order layout; a default/preorder node inside a topological depset is not reversed (run 1 r_topo MISMATCH; native flatten fixed; orders=/deep= probes equal in run 2).
key_findings.struct_dedup: struct() values and provider instances with equal fields (same provider) deduplicate across direct, transitive and targets; struct() never equals a provider instance; both share the element type struct.
key_findings.gaps: Bazel accepts frozen lists and lambdas inside depset elements (outputs recorded in G/*); native fails explicitly.

key_findings: Frozen lists/dicts inside struct elements (from a dependency provider or a loaded .bzl global) are accepted by Bazel; native owned snapshots match repr, ==, `in`, dedup (list never equals tuple; dicts equal regardless of insertion order, first kept) and to_list() re-allocates them frozen: append/pop/setdefault fail with "trying to mutate a frozen list/dict value" (E/df_append*, E/df_dict_*). Top-level frozen list/dict stay "depsets cannot contain items of type ..." (E/df_top_*).

Single-transitive identity shortcut: depset(transitive=[x]), [depset(), x], [x, depset(order=topological)], [x, x], chains, depset([1], transitive=[depset([1])]) and topological same-order are the same depset (==, in, dict keys, struct/depset dedup); a compatible-but-different order, two distinct sets, or a direct element not equal to a singleton make a new depset (//df:report).

Empty transitive depsets are skipped before type and order checks (a typed empty target.files with string direct elements is accepted); non-empty ones are type-checked before order-checked; the text is "Order 'preorder' is incompatible with order 'postorder'" (E/df_order_*).
Depsets are hashable (identity) in Bazel; native now implements write_hash consistently with Depset ==.
